To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATRA and poly(I:C) synergize in the activation of melanoma cells and that this synergism is controlled by both TLR3 and the MDA5 pathway.
ATRA and polyIC induce chemokine secretion and migration of antigen-presenting cells in human melanoma cells via TLR3 and/or MDA5.

combined ATRA and poly I:C treatment results in strong, MDA5/TLR3-dependent chemokine and interferon &bgra; responses in cultured melanoma cells, and that this treatment modality triggers a functional migrational response in professional antigen presenting cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel treatment modalities for melanoma, the most aggressive form of skin cancer.

the question whether a temporally designed treatment of human melanomas with ATRA and the TLR3 agonist polyI:C results, in an enhanced TLR3 and/or MDA5-mediated response in human melanoma cell cultures.
the question of whether the combination of two different immunomodulatory compounds (ATRA and polyI:C) can be used to improve melanoma therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ATRA and poly I:C treatment of human melanomas in vitro is a temporally designed treatment option for melanoma patients.
ATRA and poly I:C treatment of melanoma results in a strong, TLR/MDA5 mediated chemokine and INF response which triggers a migratory response in antigen presenting cells.
ATRA and poly I:C are strong inducers for chemokines and IFNβ secretion in both WM983A and WM35 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment with polyI:C and ATRA in combination can induce a stronger response than the treatment with each agent alone in human melanoma cells.
ATRA and poly I:C can be used to enhance melanoma cell killing and to stimulate immune cells to migrate to the melanoma cells.
the treatment of human melanomas with ATRA followed by polyI:C is a promising approach for future melanoma therapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combined treatment with all-trans retinoic (ATRA) acid and polyinosinic-polycytidylic (polyI:C), a synthetic analogue of dsRNA, results in enhanced secretion of chemokines and IFNβ in human melanoma cell lines in vitro.
the combination of ATRA and poly I:C treatment is more effective than either treatment alone in the activation of TLR3/MAVS and MDA5/MAVS signaling in melanoma cells.
ATRA treatment followed by polyI:C treatment results in strong TLR3 and/or MDA5-mediated chemokines and IFNβ responses in melanoma cells.
